item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-bf129d1277a74da0","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"SIPRI reports that Mexico's military expenditure reached $11.8 billion in 2023, down 1.5% from 2022 but 55% above 2014; National Guard allocations rose from 0.7% of military expenditure in 2019 to 11% in 2023. SIPRI characterizes the regional use of militaries against criminal gangs as often more violent than conventional responses.","question_ids":["2B.8","3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 military expenditure and National Guard allocation; the interpretation of effects is SIPRI's broader regional assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern Mexico during López Obrador's presidency, but the source does not attribute the spending decisions personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not provide Mexican military outcomes, civilian-harm figures, procurement details, or evidence of López Obrador's personal authorization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55da4b64bf8b6fb3","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Integralia's four-year indicator report records declines from 2018 to 2022 in democracy measures, presidential approval, subjective well-being, and an increase in the party's governorships from 4 to 20; it also reports corruption prevalence and cost increasing between 2017 and 2021.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","5B.5","6B.5","7B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report predates 2023 and compares 2018-2022 or 2017-2021; it provides background relevant to the 2023 period, not a 2023 endpoint.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates aggregate indicators during López Obrador's administration but expressly says it does not assess or conclude on government performance.","limitations":["Indicators are national aggregates and do not establish causation or personal responsibility.","The report's stated purpose is descriptive, not evaluative."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55da4b64bf8b6fb3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Integralia reports that by 2022 unemployment was nearly unchanged from 2018, formal IMSS-affiliated jobs and the minimum wage increased, while inflation rose from 4.9% to 8.4%, public investment fell 17.1%, private investment fell 8.8%, public debt rose from 44.9% to 48.9% of GDP, and Pemex production fell 11.6%.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Evidence covers 2018-2022 and predates 2023; it is contextual rather than a direct 2023 measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe outcomes during López Obrador's administration but do not isolate presidential causation from external or institutional factors.","limitations":["No policy implementation detail or distributional breakdown beyond the listed indicators.","No direct evidence of 2023 adaptation or correction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55da4b64bf8b6fb3","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Integralia reports that social-protection expenditure increased 34.9% from 2018 to 2022 and the senior-citizens program budget increased 382.5%, while educational lag was nearly unchanged, lack of access to health services rose from 16.2% to 28.2%, poverty rose from 41.9% to 43.9%, extreme poverty rose from 7.0% to 8.5%, and life expectancy fell from 75.0 to 70.2 years between 2018 and 2021.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers 2018-2022, with some social indicators ending in 2020 or 2021; it is background for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures occurred during López Obrador's administration, but the report does not establish that he personally caused the changes.","limitations":["The report does not assess service quality, targeting, exclusion, or policy lag in detail.","Pandemic and other external shocks complicate attribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55da4b64bf8b6fb3","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Integralia reports that from 2018 to 2022 intentional homicide declined 10.3% and total thefts declined 27.8%, but extortion rose 54.3%, retail drug dealing rose 42.7%, impunity remained very high, the global Rule of Law Index declined 6.7%, and journalist assassinations rose from 8 to 11.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","7B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The comparison is 2018-2022, with some data ending in 2021; it does not directly measure 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe national conditions under López Obrador but do not establish personal responsibility or policy causation.","limitations":["Reported crime, impunity, and press-violence indicators have measurement and reporting limitations.","No evidence here on specific orders, investigations, remedies, or 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35d664c0c6e1f4f3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A Yucatán judge provisionally suspended construction of Tren Maya section 5 between Playa del Carmen and Tulum because work began without the required environmental-impact authorization; scientists, environmentalists, archaeologists, and cave divers warned of risks to forests, caves, cenotes, and underground rivers. The government had designated the project as a national-security matter to accelerate construction.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","4B.9","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The event occurred in April 2022, before the target year, but concerns and institutional choices remained relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The project was López Obrador's flagship work; the article attributes the national-security designation and government defense of the project to his administration.","limitations":["This is a single reported judicial suspension and does not establish the final legal or environmental outcome.","The article includes reported claims by interested parties and does not independently quantify environmental damage."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9cc08b09cdaa2a88","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A Sedena document leak reportedly showed that the army contracted with Comercializadora Antsua in 2019 for Pegasus-related software, while leaked records described monitoring of politicians, journalists, feminists, Zapatistas, guerrillas, and human-rights defenders. López Obrador denied spying on journalists or opponents and distinguished intelligence from espionage; organizations reported Pegasus infections of at least three people during his administration.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reporting is from October 2022 but concerns alleged conduct during 2019-2022 and remained directly relevant to accountability and surveillance questions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador publicly denied the conduct and claimed a commitment that no opponent would be spied on; the reported contracts and operational conduct are attributed to Sedena rather than proven to have been personally ordered by him.","limitations":["The article reports leaked documents and allegations; it does not establish a final judicial finding or presidential knowledge.","The source does not report a completed remedy or independent investigation outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35b98a1eefe2037c","start_unit":20,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"CPJ reported that from March 2023 López Obrador sharply criticized Artículo 19, Proceso, Animal Político, Aristegui Noticias, and journalist Nayeli Roldán over reporting on alleged illegal government surveillance. The targets reported online abuse, threats, misogynistic insults, and increased insecurity; CPJ also reported that López Obrador denied illegal spyware operations, called critical media tendentious or bought, and did not correct alleged false information. CPJ stated that Mexico was the Western Hemisphere's most violent country for journalism in 2022, with at least three journalists killed in retaliation and ten additional cases under investigation.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers López Obrador's conduct and reported effects in 2023, while the journalist-killing comparison is for 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The public criticisms and statements are directly attributed to López Obrador; online abuse and threats are reported by the targeted journalists and organizations, not proven as personally ordered by him.","limitations":["CPJ reports allegations and interview accounts; it does not establish that López Obrador intended or directed the subsequent threats.","The source does not provide a completed investigation or remedy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-64463396d57214a7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"WOLA reported that López Obrador moved from campaign promises to return the army to its barracks toward expanding and making military public-security deployment effectively permanent, placing the National Guard under Sedena operational control and proposing legislative changes contrary to the Constitution's civilian designation. WOLA also reported reduced absolute levels of some serious human-rights violations and fewer armed confrontations, but continuing excessive-force and arbitrary-killing cases, weak accountability, refusal to comply with an Inter-American Court oversight ruling, and insufficient investment in civilian criminal-justice institutions.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.8","2B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published in September 2022; it describes policy direction and outcomes during López Obrador's administration that continued into the 2023 target period.","ruler_attribution":"WOLA directly attributes the National Guard proposal, military-deployment policy, and stated instructions to López Obrador.","limitations":["WOLA's assessment is an expert interview and advocacy analysis rather than a court finding.","The source gives limited quantitative evidence for 2023 and does not establish personal responsibility for individual abuses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69497064d8f46c83","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A 2022 cyberattack exposed more than four million Sedena emails and demonstrated a major digital-security failure. Experts attributed weak protection partly to austerity, insufficient cybersecurity staffing and technology, and institutional fragmentation; López Obrador acknowledged the hack but did not address the cybersecurity weakness or announce a remedy in the reported remarks. The army had also received expanded state responsibilities, including customs and major infrastructure.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","4B.4","4B.5","5B.6","6B.6","7B.2","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The breach occurred in September 2022; the exposed institutional weakness and reported lack of corrective response are relevant to the 2023 posture.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the expansion of military responsibilities and the president's response to López Obrador; expert explanations of the cybersecurity failure are not proof of his personal intent.","limitations":["The article does not establish the complete budgetary or administrative causes of the breach.","It reports no later 2023 remediation outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cf5d27f45043b563","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A 2023 El País opinion article argues that López Obrador expanded the armed forces' control over ports, airports, customs, security, infrastructure, and strategic enterprises, while favoring military secrecy over truth and justice for Ayotzinapa victims. It also alleges weak accountability for victims, excessive empowerment of the military, pressure on judicial and autonomous oversight institutions, and inadequate response to killings of police, activists, and other victims.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.8","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in October 2023 and directly concerns the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The article directly attributes the described military transfers, secrecy posture, and institutional choices to López Obrador.","limitations":["The article is explicitly opinion and contains interpretation and rhetorical claims.","Several assertions are not accompanied by primary records or quantified evidence in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-70c632cb0649404a","start_unit":1,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The United States requested USMCA consultations alleging that Mexico's energy measures favored CFE and Pemex over private and U.S. firms. The measures included priority dispatch for CFE, delays or denials of private permits, a Pemex-only extension for ultra-low-sulfur diesel compliance, and a 2022 strategy favoring CFE/Pemex gas supplies and restricting U.S. natural-gas imports; the United States alleged discrimination and inconsistent, non-impartial administration.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10","7B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The request was issued in July 2022, but the challenged measures and their implementation were relevant during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The document attributes the measures to Mexico's government and legal instruments during López Obrador's administration, but does not establish that he personally directed each measure.","limitations":["This is a U.S. government allegation in a trade-consultation request, not a final USMCA ruling.","The source does not report the ultimate dispute outcome or actual economic effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b07f75d587c498a3","start_unit":13,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that López Obrador and legislators from his coalition effectively paralyzed INAI by leaving three commissioner seats vacant; after López Obrador vetoed two appointments and his party rejected another proposal, INAI lacked the five commissioners needed to meet or issue decisions and had 3,947 pending cases. HRW also reported repeated proposals to eliminate the agency, a national-security infrastructure order overturned by the Supreme Court, and a substantially similar order issued afterward.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","6B.5","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the institutional situation in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"HRW directly attributes the paralysis, veto, elimination proposals, and repeated infrastructure secrecy orders to López Obrador and legislators from his coalition.","limitations":["The source is an HRW news release and does not establish the president's subjective motive.","It does not report the eventual resolution of the pending appointments or complaint."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-ba8384e3215a60f0","SRC-31223442a4832885"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is uneven in period coverage: several documents concern 2022 or earlier conditions rather than direct 2023 observations.","Reported allegations, advocacy analyses, and opinion pieces are identified as such and are not treated as final adjudications.","No facts are scored."]}
